name: Texas
basePeriod: The first four of the last five completed calendar quarters before your claim's effective date.
notModeled: Claims with an effective date before October 4, 2026 use the previous range, $75 to $605.
The alternate base period, which Texas allows only after a medically verifiable illness or injury.
A second benefit year's extra test: six times the new weekly benefit earned since the last claim began.

citation.sourceDocument: Texas Workforce Commission, Eligibility & Benefit Amounts; Texas Labor Code §§207.002, 207.005, 207.006, 207.021
citation.sourceNote: Labor Code §207.002(a): benefits are "1/25 of the wages received ... during that quarter in the individual's base period in which wages were highest." §207.006: a benefit rate that "is not a multiple of $1" is "increased to the next multiple of $1." TWC's page says it divides by 25 "and round[s] to the nearest dollar"; the statute's upward rounding is used here, and the two differ by at most $1 a week. §207.005: the total "may not exceed the lesser of: (1) 26 times the individual's benefit amount; or (2) 27 percent of the individual's benefit wage credits." §207.021(a)(6): wages "in at least two calendar quarters" and "not less than 37 times the individual's benefit amount." The minimum and maximum are indexed each year (47.6% and 7.6% of the state average weekly wage, §207.002(b)); TWC's table gives $76 and $619 from October 4, 2026, and $75 and $605 from October 5, 2025. Texas pays no dependent allowance. Read on 2026-10-19.
